title: What almost four million New York requests reveal
changes: A result-first, continuous data-explorer treatment informed by a sampled visual study of Parker Prompts' cinematic tutorial and three supplementary transcripts. Original, deterministic graphics replace repeated still screenshots. All values derive from retained NYC Open Data queries. No creator footage, likeness, voice, proprietary prompt kit, generated film or music is reused.

beats.text: Almost four million New York requests. The biggest category wasn't noise.
Illegal parking came first. Six hundred eleven thousand, two hundred eighty two requests.
I analyzed one year of three one one data. Here is the exact date window.
Then I filtered residential noise and grouped the requests by hour.
The peak is ten to eleven at night. Sunday has the most requests.
Heat follows a different pattern. Switch the same view to monthly requests.
January is around twenty two times August. And exactly one request was filed under trapping pigeon.
Requests aren't unique incidents. Keep the queries and results with the chart, so anyone can check the story.
